chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Favorite jamming places in 1930s Los Angeles
summary: Jam spots on Central Avenue and the changing street numbers.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You mention [LaGranda] Mason and [LaGrande Mason's brother, what was his name?
Besides upstairs at the Alabam, where were the favorite jamming places in the thirties in Los Angeles?

Oh, wow. I can't remember the name. It was a restaurant, oh, wow, you really caught me off base. It was a restuarant and we use to go in the back after it was closed. And then there was another place --
The restaurant was between 42nd and 43rd on Central. And then there was another restaurant -- see they changed the streets over there.
They put in a street, didn't they?

Because when I went -- when I first came to Los Angeles. The street I lived on was 40th, that was the street that the Downbeat Corner was on. And then they changed that to 41st, you know. So if I mislead you in streets, it's not my fault, it's the City Planner. (Laughter).
Yeah I know, between Santa Barbara and Vernon I think they added a street and changed the numbers.
